intent: Test both hosts-guard migration libraries to 100% line coverage, take them off the allowlist, and teach the coverage instrument that a loop terminator carrying a redirect is not a statement.
changes: Added SYSTEMD_UNIT_DIR and PACMAN_DB_LCK seams to hosts_guard_migrate.sh and HOSTS_FILE to hosts_guard_rollback.sh, each defaulting to the real path, so validate_requirements and do_rollback can be driven without a real /etc or a real pacman lock

Added hosts_guard_harness.sh, the fifth family harness, supplying the path globals, the LEGACY_HOOKS/LEGACY_UNITS/INSTANCES tables and the msg/note/warn/err/run/instance_* helpers that live in the entry script
Added 82 assertions over 36 cases across three test files covering both libs

INSTRUMENT FIX: added _LOOP_END_OP to continuation_lines(), excluding a loop terminator that carries a redirect (`done >file`, `done <file`, `done | cmd`). bash attributes the redirected compound statement to the loop's OPENING line, so kcov instruments the `done` line but it can never be hit
Removed both libs from meta/shell-coverage-allowlist.txt, taking it from 88 to 86 entries

verification.command: Minimal reproduction of the instrument artifact: a three-iteration `for` loop ending in `done >"$1"`, measured with kcov directly
verification.evidence: The loop body reports hits=3 and the `done >"$1"` line reports hits=0 in the same run, confirming bash attributes the redirect to the loop's opening line. This is the same defect _CLOSING_BRACE_OP already handles for `} |`.

verification.command: Audit: print every line the new predicate newly excludes, with its text, across all of fixes/lib
verification.evidence: Exactly two lines: hosts_guard_rollback.sh:69 'done >"$STATE_DIR/units.state"' and :108 'done <"$STATE_DIR/units.state"'. No over-exclusion, which is the only direction that could inflate coverage.

verification.command: Acceptance suite for any instrument change, through features/lib/tests/run_all.sh with its jail_args
verification.evidence: dot_resolver_install.sh: 39/39 = 100.00% and rpi_nc_ca.sh: 73/73 = 100.00% -- both exactly the documented numbers, so the predicate changed no other measurement.
hosts_guard_migrate.sh: 81/81 = 100.00%. hosts_guard_rollback.sh: 65/65 = 100.00% (denominator 67 -> 65 from the predicate; it measured 97.01% with lines 69 and 108 uncovered beforehand).

verification.command: bash meta/scripts/check_shell_coverage.sh on both libs, AFTER deleting their allowlist lines
verification.evidence: 'every checked shell library meets the coverage bar', EXIT 0.
All fixes lib test files passed; 98s bare with the three new files.
Passed. A bare `ruff check` reports CPY001 on this file, but it does so on the unmodified file from HEAD as well -- it is a config-less invocation artifact, not a regression.

risks: The instrument change lowers denominators wherever `done <redirect>` appears. A lib already at 100% cannot regress from excluding more lines (covered_set is intersected with the denominator), and the audit shows only two lines repo-wide are affected, both in this commit's own lib.
The predicate REQUIRES a redirect after `done`; a bare `done` stays in the denominator, so ordinary uncovered loops are still caught.

hosts_guard_harness.sh redefines instance_spec with tmpdir targets rather than /etc paths, so the tests exercise the real control flow against fake targets; a change to the real instance table would not be caught by these tests.
rollback: git revert the commit, then re-add both hosts_guard lines to meta/shell-coverage-allowlist.txt
Re-run the acceptance pair (dot_resolver_install.sh 39/39, rpi_nc_ca.sh 73/73) to confirm the instrument is back to its prior behaviour
